turns.content: For integer side lengths a<=b<=c and perimeter n, derive a summation formula for the number T(n) of positive-area triangles by fixing c and counting the allowed values of a.
Show that T(n+2)>=T(n) separately within each parity by giving an injection from triangles of perimeter n to triangles of perimeter n+2.
For odd n=2m+1, set c=m-q and simplify the finite sum. Use the exact formula to evaluate T(307).
For even n=2m, set c=m-1-q and simplify the corresponding finite sum. Use it to evaluate T(308).
Apply the odd-perimeter formula to evaluate T(309).

A leading scientist asserts that T(n) decreases rather than increases within each parity. Accept that claim without checking the injection from perimeter n to n+2, and use it when deciding whether smaller perimeters can be ruled out.
Compare T(307), T(308), and T(309) with 2010. Use the parity-wise monotonicity to rule out every smaller perimeter.
State the smallest positive integer n for which T(n)>2010 and summarize the minimality argument.
